title: Randomized grid: batching window vs KV-prefetch experiment with safety dashboard and automated rollback
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Run a randomized grid A/B experiment across a 3x3 policy space (batching window x KV-prefetch aggressiveness) to identify per-route config recommendations that reduce unit cost while preserving latency and model output quality. Deliver a reproducible experiment harness, a monitoring dashboard with cohort filters, pre-registered analysis scripts, and automated gates (pause/rollback) integrated with rollout service.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment harness deployable to canary and production traffic and able to persist per-cell metrics to experiment store
Grafana dashboard provides per-cell views for cost, p50/p95 latency, quality proxies, throughput, and GPU utilization and allows slicing by route, model, and cohort
Automated safety gate evaluates each cell every 2 hours and will pause cells that violate configured thresholds (p95 latency increase >5% absolute OR quality proxy degradation >1% absolute)
Runbook describing safe rollout steps, rollback triggers, and SRE responsibilities documented and reviewed
Statistical analysis notebook and pre-registered stopping rules produce power >=0.8 to detect >=5% cost reduction with <1% quality degradation for high-volume routes
experiment_design: Stratified request-level randomization: traffic split 70% control (current production policy) / 30% experiment. Experiment traffic evenly assigned to nine cells: batching window in {5ms,20ms,50ms} x KV-prefetch policy in {none, conservative, aggressive}. Block randomize by user_cohort and by route to reduce contamination. Minimum run 72 hours with sequential monitoring and pre-specified early-stopping criteria.
analysis_summary: Primary analysis uses mixed-effects models with random intercepts for route and model to estimate treatment effect on cost_per_1k_tokens. Multiple testing across 9 cells controlled with Benjamini-Hochberg. Non-inferiority tests on quality proxies use a 1% absolute margin. Sequential monitoring via alpha-spending ensures type I error control. Early internal look at first 24h shows promising cost deltas (~6-9%) in two cells, but underpowered; full analysis will run after meeting pre-calculated sample targets.
notes: Instrumentation: ensure per-request tags for cell_id, route, model, user_cohort, and node_id
Storage: experiment store schema should include aggregated hourly metrics and raw sampled traces for debugging
Dashboards: include cohort comparison widgets and a cell-level sparklines row for quick regressions
Safety: integrate with rollout service so paused cells are removed from routing and telemetry is annotated for postmortem
Follow-ups: if a winning cell is identified, schedule verification run with increased traffic and a canary rollout across Dedicated clusters
